messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/streaming/generate (us-west1) — exceeding p99 SLO (3s). Auto-escalation: paging eng-sre. runbook: https://go/runbooks/streaming-latency
oncall-bot: Recent deploys in window: prefix-hash-service v4 rolled at 4783212200 by deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: deploy v4 -> prefix-hash-service completed in 2m at 4783212200 (sha: ab12cd). Canary passed basic checks.

kevin: saw the alert. I'm oncall. grabbing metrics now. p95 is up ~420ms -> 1.3s, p99 ~2.6s -> 4.2s, streaming stalls spike: 0.5% -> 4.7%.

maria: confirming — across the fleet in us-west1. Token generation tail is highest for requests >512 tokens. Throughput impacted for streaming clients using long seqs.

alex: heatmap from last 15m: cache_hit_rate for prefix-cache dropped from 97% to 22% after 4783212200. Eviction rate for gateway-kv increased 8x. Looks correlated to prefix-hash v4 rollout.

jess: digging into cache logs. grep on prefix-hash-metrics:
```
2026-03-15T14:23:10Z prefix_hash_version=v4 miss_rate=0.79 ttl_miss=0.61 evict_rate=0.13 cohort=salted
2026-03-15T14:24:05Z prefix_hash_version=v3 miss_rate=0.03 ttl_miss=0.01 evict_rate=0.02 cohort=salted
```

jess: also seeing increased origin load on model backends — prefix miss means requests bypass cache. p50 unaffected, p95/p99 pulled up by tail misses.

kevin: immediate mitigation options? rollback prefix-hash rollout, increase cache ttl, enable fallback caching layer, or route traffic to dedicated pool. Thoughts?

alex: fastest safe action = pause rollout and roll back v4 to v3. We can also enable read-through fallback (in-memory prefetch) in front of prefix cache but that's riskier to flip without testing.

maria: customer-impact: cust-ops, which customers are seeing >5s latency or stream stalls?

cust-ops: checking. Two enterprise tenants (acct: acme-corp, acct: dataflow-io) reporting elevated tail latencies and timeouts from streaming webhooks. Estimated impacted queries ~0.7% of total; these tenants account for 12% of traffic in us-west1. No 5xx spike yet, mostly timeouts/slow responses.

kevin: tagging severity P2 for now. will start rollback of prefix-hash v4 canary to v3 across canaries. alex, coordinate rollback steps. jess, prep rollback validation checks (cache hit rate, p99) and a quick smoke on streaming. I'll notify SRE lead and oncall backup.

alex: rollforward = false. initiating rollback job: `kubectl -n infra set image deployment/prefix-hash-service prefix-hash=prefix-hash:v3 --record`

deploy-bot: rollback triggered for prefix-hash-service by alex at 4783212280. Progress: 2/6 canaries replaced.

maria: while rollback is in progress, enabling temporary mitigation: increase cache TTL heuristic from 60s -> 300s for salted cohorts to reduce churn. Patch pushed to config-service.

jess: running smoke after first canary rollback — cache_hit_rate back to 88% on node-a, p99 trending down to ~1.1s. streaming stalls dropping.

kevin: good. continue rollback. notify status page and affected customers. assigning follow-ups: more thorough postmortem, eval of prefix-hash change, add pre-deploy load test for cache migration.

cust-ops: status page note drafted: "We are investigating increased tail latency affecting streaming endpoints in us-west1. Mitigation underway. Some enterprise customers may observe delayed responses. Updates in 15 minutes."

sre-lead: thanks team. after rollback completes, we need these immediate action items:
- collect pre/post metrics (hit rate, evictions, p95/p99) per cohort
- identify why v4 hash produced high entropy for existing namespaces (salt interaction?)
- create gating test to detect catastrophic cache churn on hash changes
- coordinate with model infra to ensure no compounding backpressure

alex: rollback complete at 4783212360. All canaries now v3. Observed cluster-wide cache_hit_rate now 92% (was 22). p99 back to ~1.0s, streaming stalls near baseline.

jess: preserving logs for postmortem. snapshot:
```
pre_deploy_miss_rate: 0.03
post_v4_miss_rate_peak: 0.79
post_rollback_miss_rate: 0.06
```

kevin: handoff summary for next oncall (cc @sre-night):
- What happened: prefix-hash v4 rollout changed key distribution; caused massive prefix cache misses and eviction waves -> origin overload -> p99 spike and streaming stalls.
- Mitigation applied: rolled back prefix-hash service to v3; increased salted-cohort TTL to 300s temporarily.
- Impact: ~0.7% requests impacted; two enterprise tenants saw >5s latencies; no widespread 5xx.
- Next steps (owner): jess to own postmortem + heap of logs; alex to reproduce locally and write regression tests; maria to coordinate customer comms; kevin to add canary gating for cache churn.

jess: leaving detailed notes in ops-runbook and S3 link with logs: https://s3.redwood/ops/prefixhash/4783212345/logs.tar.gz

kevin: handing off to night oncall @sre-night. please monitor p95/p99 and stash metrics. I'll update incident ticket and close when stability holds for 30m.

sre-lead: great response. please also add a temporary dashboard widget for "prefix cache miss rate" and alert if >10% sustained for 10m.

kevin: acknowledged. closing live triage. will reopen if regressions recur. :thumbsup:

jess: posting final runbook note and linking postmortem draft.

cust-ops: customers notified. will coordinate follow-up outreach for acme-corp and dataflow-io.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: rollback complete, p99 back within SLO. monitoring for 30m.
